methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: A regional college launching an AI workforce lab signals distributed capability-building outside major metros, creating peer learning infrastructure that could spread deep AI fluency through workforce networks rather than concentrating in NoVA/Richmond hubs.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops explicitly targeting the technology gap represent grassroots distribution of AI literacy outside the NoVA corridor, building local capacity through peer networks rather than platform dependency or metro concentration.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership creates deep institutional AI capability in Richmond, but the metro-anchored model risks replicating the NoVA concentration pattern rather than distributing capability to underserved regions like Southside or Southwest.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Data center infrastructure concentrating in NoVA without corresponding workforce development or regional distribution mechanisms deepens the urban-rural divide, creating physical AI infrastructure in one region while capability gaps widen elsewhere.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech adding an AI minor creates deep technical capability in the New River Valley but as a traditional academic program may concentrate expertise among credentialed students rather than distributing fluency broadly through workforce and community networks.
